description: Natural placement of the v2_2 vocal (first AI take, separated stem) on the new song form: cut, raised-cosine fades, integer-sample shifts and ONE global gain only. No pitch processing, no time processing, no resampling.
not_verified_by_ear: Everything here is measured by code; nobody listened to the result.

schema.time_base: src_* = seconds on the timeline of yeni4/vokal/kaynak/v2_2_vokal.wav (= v2_2.mp3); dest_* = seconds on the timeline of vokal_dogal.wav (0.100 s lead-in, bar n downbeat at 0.100 + n * 2.285714)
schema.pieces[]: the 21 placed chunks (3 per verse: P1 = L1, P2 = L2, P3 = 'diye bağırır' + L4). src_in/src_out, dest_in/dest_out = extent of the audio INCLUDING the fades; dest_bar_downbeat = bar line the piece is anchored to; parts[] = the contiguous audio parts actually copied (two for the repaired K3_P2); fade_* = raised-cosine fades at the piece edges
schema.lines[]: the 28 sung lines (L1, L2, diye, L4 per verse). dest_bar = the bar the line is sung in (L4 = the bar after 'diye'); src_start/src_end = acoustic start / end from the segmentation; onset_minus_expected_beat_ms = where the first sound falls relative to its beat (negative = before)

lines[].syllables[].text, word: kept syllables only (229); the excised extra nucleus of verse 3 is listed under repairs
lines[].syllables[].src_start/src_end, dest_start/dest_end: syllable boundaries from the segmentation (dest = src + shift of the piece)
lines[].syllables[].midi: ORIGINAL sung pitch: median f0 over the syllable core (MIDI, A4 = 69 = 440 Hz)
lines[].syllables[].pitch_start / pitch_mid / pitch_end: medians over the first quarter / middle half / last quarter of the core frames (MIDI)
lines[].syllables[].dest_nucleus, dest_core_start/end: nucleus = instant of the envelope PEAK of the vowel (not its onset); core = the voiced core used for the pitch medians; both on the destination timeline
lines[].syllables[].dest_bar, beat_in_bar, dest_grid_time: the grid slot of the syllable in the new form (sixteenth-note grid of the segmentation) and its time
lines[].syllables[].start_minus_grid_ms: syllable start (its consonant) against the grid slot; negative = starts before the beat so that the vowel lands on it
lines[].syllables[].notes[]: stable note plateaus inside the syllable
lines[].syllables[].boundary_flag: true = a boundary of this syllable was placed on the beat grid by the segmentation (li|ğin, di|ye)

schema.syllables_flat[]: the same 229 kept syllables as one flat table (verse, line, piece, text, src/dest start and end, median MIDI, start / mid / end pitch, bar and beat slot); lines[].syllables[] has the full detail
schema.removed_animal_sounds[]: per verse the source range that was dropped (sung animal sounds) and the resulting digital silence in the destination
schema.animal_call_slots[]: where the real animal calls go (40 ms before the downbeats of bars 3 and 4 of the verse) and the margins to the vocal
schema.repairs[]: edits other than plain cutting and shifting
schema.open_questions[]: things measured but deliberately NOT changed

audio.silence: exact digital zero outside the placed parts
audio.processing: cut + raised-cosine fades + integer-sample shift + one global gain; no pitch shift, no time stretch, no resampling
audio.source: yeni4/vokal/kaynak/v2_2_vokal.wav (mono 44.1 kHz 24-bit, UVR-MDX-NET-Voc_FT stem, sample-aligned with v2_2.mp3)

placement_rule.how: the source bar line (constant machine lattice of the mp3: lattice.json, 105.002798 BPM, beat n at 0.00011546 + n * 0.5714133459 s; verse v downbeat = beat 15 + 24 (v-1)) is mapped onto the destination bar line: dest_time = dest_bar_downbeat + (src_time - src_bar_downbeat), rounded to whole samples
placement_rule.anchors: P1: source bar 0 of the verse -> bar 0 of the verse; P2: source bar 1 -> bar 2; P3: source bar 2 (the bar that contains 'diye') -> bar 5, so 'diye' lands on beat 2 of bar 5 and L4 on bar 6
placement_rule.tempo_difference: source lattice 105.002798 BPM, destination 105.000 BPM: 0.061 ms per bar; no stretch is applied, so L4 (one bar after P3's anchor) sits 0.061 ms early against its own bar line
placement_rule.fades: all cut points are the segmentation's (kesim.json pieces[]) and so are the fade lengths, with two measured exceptions: the line-2 fade-out in verses 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 (see options) and the two fades at the verse-3 excision (see repairs)
placement_rule.pickup: pieces that begin with a consonant before the bar line begin before the destination bar line by the same amount (dest_in_minus_bar_downbeat_ms)

noise_floor.in_this_file: digital zero between the pieces (the stem's residual between the verses is not copied)

options.note: line-2 fade-out in the verses where 'var' runs into the sung animal sound without a gap (1, 2, 3, 6, 7): 30 ms instead of the segmentation's 25 ms, because the envelope then falls (-3 -> -15 dB) in 14 ms median instead of 11 ms, closer to this singer's natural word endings (15.5-27.3 ms at the seven 'var,' of line 1); cost: 'var' is 2.5 ms shorter at the half-amplitude point. The fade always ends at var_end. Rebuild with --l2-gecis-ms 25 for the segmentation's value.

repairs.type: excision of an extra sung syllable (no pitch or time processing)
repairs.what: the singer sang 'a-tı-la-rı' (four nuclei); the extra nucleus (a bright vowel of 82 ms + a sustained /l/ of 180 ms on its own note E4, on beat 6.5) is cut out; what remains is 'at' + rest + 'ları'

evidence.verdict: FOUR syllable nuclei were sung (a - tı - la - rı), not three (at - la - rı): the user's impression 'atıları' is confirmed.

excision.start_definition: quietest instant between the end of the /t/ frication and the onset of voicing (5 ms RMS -39.7 dBFS)
excision.end_definition: 55 ms before the onset of the 'a' of 'la' (F2-band rise): keeps a normal-length /l/ in front of 'a'

fade_out_before.why: 15 ms instead of 5 ms: it starts after the end of the /t/ frication (39.7357) and only covers the residual noise at -36..-41 dBFS; reaches exact zero at the excision start

natural_onset_rise_10_90_ms.definition: 100-1000 Hz band, 3 ms RMS envelope, rise from 10 % to 90 % of the level 15-35 ms after voicing starts, at this singer's voicing onsets after voiceless consonants (çift|li, nek|le, ...)

fade_in_after.why: 30 ms centred on the recommended splice point instead of 10 ms after it: this singer's own voiced onsets after voiceless consonants rise (10-90 %) in 18 ms median (n=24, quartiles 15-23 ms), which equals a 31 ms raised cosine; a 10 ms fade (6 ms rise) would be at the hardest end of that range. The /l/ still lasts 55 ms from the half-amplitude point to the vowel 'a'.

silence_inside_word.note: exact digital zero; from the end of the vowel 'a' of 'at' (39.5800) to the half-amplitude point of the /l/ there are 386 ms without voicing, with the /t/ release (39.6639-39.7357) in between

rhythm.option: A (gap left open, recommended by the segmentation)
rhythm.note: every remaining sample keeps its original time; 'var' stays exactly in time

repairs.not_verified_by_ear: that 'at' + an eighth-note rest + 'ları' sounds natural was not checked by listening

open_questions.what: verse 7 line 4 'çift' is sung on A#3 (MIDI 58.27), 3.6 semitones below the other verses (80 ms vowel)
open_questions.decision: NOT changed: no pitch processing is allowed in this step and the segmentation did not recommend a repair; a short low pickup into the leap to G4. The pitch step ('ezgi') retunes it anyway.

open_questions.what: verse 7 line 1 'nın' sags from A4 to about F4 (median G4, 1.8 semitones below the other verses)
verse 3 line 4 'çift' sags from MIDI 61.9 to 59.9 inside the syllable
in verses 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 'var' runs into the sung animal sound without any low point: line 2 is cut at full level with a 30 ms fade ending exactly at var_end
open_questions.decision: cut point as recommended by the segmentation; nothing after var_end is kept. In the mix the real animal call starts 20-37 ms after the cut, and a light reverb on the vocal bus would give these endings a tail. Whether they sound clipped was not checked by ear.

open_questions.what: breaths / pre-phonation before line 1 of verses 1-3 (peak -35 .. -46 dBFS) and a puff after the last word of verse 2 (31.45-31.60 s, peak -31 dBFS)
open_questions.decision: NOT included (default cuts of the segmentation); alternatives are in kesim.json (breath_before.cut_in_with_breath, after_sound.cut_out_including_after_sound)

open_questions.what: 16 syllable boundaries have no acoustic mark and sit on the beat grid (14 x li|ğin in 'çiftliğinde', 2 x di|ye in verses 4 and 7)
open_questions.decision: no audio consequence here (nothing is cut there); it only matters for per-syllable pitch processing in the 'ezgi' step

open_questions.what: the pieces are continuous stretches of the separated stem, so whatever the separator left of the old D-minor band inside the sung bars is still inside them
open_questions.decision: not treated here (no filtering or gating inside the pieces)
